about: Acceptance catalogue (docs/ACCEPTANCE.md). Our own text; game data is referred to by name only. Read by scripts/acceptance.ps1.

groups.title: HUD and command bar on the original layouts
World rendering: terrain, roads, objects, light, fog

shell-30.title: Main menu at 30 Hz (old saved game)

hud-tour.title: Command bar: idle, selection, construction menu, queue, tooltip, game menu

hud-multiselect.title: Command bar with several units selected

skirmish.title: Skirmish on Alpine Assault (America against China)

skirmish-classic.title: Skirmish with the original's mouse setup

skirmish-autoplay.title: Skirmish, the computer plays both sides (a picture every 16 seconds)

placement.title: Choosing a building site: legal spot

placement-refused.title: Choosing a building site: refused spot

jet-strafe-target.title: Jets: the attack on the missile infantry

exit-america-warfactory.title: Factory exit of the war factory, close

items.title: The installer creates a game directory
items.instruction: In the cloned repository run `pwsh scripts\install.ps1` (only if nothing lies under %LOCALAPPDATA%\CnCNew\Game yet, or to repeat it).
items.expectation: The script finds the Steam installation by itself, ends with `Installation: ...` naming content, record, client and the start line, and takes about two minutes. The Steam installation is unchanged afterwards.

items.title: Start through Start-CnCNew.cmd
items.instruction: Double-click `%LOCALAPPDATA%\CnCNew\Game\Start-CnCNew.cmd`.
items.expectation: After about half a minute of loading the main menu stands in the window, with the menu music; no console window stays open, no error message.

items.title: Uninstalling removes only our own directory
items.instruction: Only if you want to get rid of the installation: run the command.
items.expectation: content, bin, Start-CnCNew.cmd and install.json are gone; nothing outside the target directory was touched, Steam still starts the original.

items.title: Main menu: looks
items.instruction: Look at the pictures of the main menu (normal, pointer over a button, pressed).
items.expectation: Logo, frame and buttons as in the original main menu of Zero Hour; texts sit centred in the buttons and are not cut off; the button under the pointer is highlighted, the pressed one darker. (The original shows a 3D battle scene behind the menu; here the background is black - known, postponed.)

items.title: Sub-menus: single player, difficulty, challenge, briefing
items.instruction: Look at the pictures flow-single-player to flow-briefing.
items.expectation: Every page shows only its own buttons (nothing of the main menu shines through); the difficulty question has three levels as in the original; the custom-mission button is labelled and disabled.

items.title: Skirmish setup, map selection, loading screen, score screen
items.instruction: Look at the pictures flow-skirmish-setup, flow-skirmish-map-select, flow-match-loading, flow-score.
items.expectation: The setup has a preselected map and localised entries for the player slots; the map list is readable; loading and score screen are complete, without magenta or missing texts.

items.title: Options, sliders, quit dialog
items.instruction: Look at the pictures shell-options, shell-options-slider-drag, shell-quit, quitmenu.
items.expectation: The sliders are visible (a row of boxes with a handle); in the quit dialog Yes and No stand in one row and the text is easy to read.

items.title: Font and texts
items.instruction: Watch the lettering on all pictures, and flow-tooltip, hudfeedback, missiontext.
items.expectation: The lettering looks like the original's (Arial, clean edges, light text on dark ground without fringes); nothing is cut off, no text runs out of its field.

items.title: Transitions and button states in the window
items.instruction: In the main menu move the mouse over the buttons, open the single-player page and go back, open the options, drag a slider, cancel.
items.expectation: At the start and on every page change buttons and logo fade in as in the original (no hard cut); a button is lit only while the pointer is on it; the slider follows the mouse.
sources: former 60 Hz list: shell and camera

items.title: Menu music and clicks
items.instruction: Listen in the same window and click a few buttons.
items.expectation: The menu theme plays; every click on a button gives exactly one click sound; the music slider of the options changes the volume at once.

items.title: Starting a skirmish and a mission from the menu
items.instruction: Single player, skirmish, start the game; after the start Esc and exit back to the menu. Then single player, the USA campaign, pick a difficulty, start the mission, back with Esc.
items.expectation: Both start without a crash into the map with the command bar; Esc opens the game menu, exiting leads back to the main menu and the menu music sets in again.
sources: CLAUDE.md phase 16: clicking through the shell is open

items.title: A game saved at 30 Hz is refused
items.instruction: This window runs at 30 Hz: start a mission, save through Esc, quit. Then start `pwsh scripts\demo-shell.ps1` (60 Hz) and load the saved game.
items.expectation: At 60 Hz an understandable message says the game was saved at another rate, and nothing crashes; with `-TickRate 30` the same save loads.
sources: former 60 Hz list: old saved game

items.title: Command bar, idle
items.instruction: First picture of the strip (nothing selected).
items.expectation: The bar spans the whole width (at 16:9 stretched as in the original), the radar on the left, the logo of the own side on the right, the money at the top centre; no black holes.

items.title: Selection: portrait, construction menu, tooltip
items.instruction: Pictures with the dozer selected and the pointer over a construct button.
items.expectation: The unit's portrait on the right, its command buttons with their pictures in the middle; the tooltip names the building, its price and description, and for disabled buttons what is missing.

items.title: Building with a queue, money, power
items.instruction: Pictures with the war factory and the barracks selected after their orders.
items.expectation: The orders stand as pictures in the queue, the money has dropped by their price and is readable above the bar, the power bar is visible. (Known: the bar is one colour instead of the original's tiled display.)

items.title: Game menu (Esc)
items.instruction: Last pictures of the strip.
items.expectation: The translucent game menu with the logo and five buttons lies centred over the game.

items.title: Several units selected
items.instruction: Pictures with ten units selected.
items.expectation: Every selected unit carries a ring and a health bar; the bar shows the commands they share, no empty or black portrait field. (Nobody has judged this view before.)

items.title: Messages at the top left
items.instruction: In the tank duel watch the line at the top left.
items.expectation: The message (unit under attack) appears with the first hit, stands for about nine seconds and disappears; it does not flicker and does not repeat every second.

items.title: Radar
items.instruction: In the skirmish click on the radar and drag inside it.
items.expectation: The view jumps to the clicked place; own objects are coloured dots, the visible section is a frame; unexplored ground is black.

items.title: Mouse: left selects, right orders
items.instruction: Left-click a finished unit, right-click the ground; drag a box around several with the left button, order with the right; left-click on empty ground.
items.expectation: Left selects (ring, health bar), right sends the selection (a marker on the ground), a left click on empty ground clears the selection - without anything moving.

items.title: The original's mouse setup (`--mouse classic`)
items.instruction: Left-click the dozer, left-click the ground; right-click.
items.expectation: As in the unmodified original: left selects and orders, right clears the selection.

items.title: Scrolling, rotating, zooming
items.instruction: Push the pointer to every screen edge; arrow keys; hold the right button and drag; hold the middle button and drag; mouse wheel.
items.expectation: At the edge and with the arrow keys the map glides at the original's speed (at 1280 pixels width about one screen width in two seconds), not faster; the middle button rotates, the wheel zooms. Known: dragging with the right button is clearly slower than in the original.

items.title: Construction hot keys, including S, F and E
items.instruction: Select the war factory, press `S` (Sentry Drone), `C` (Crusader); select the dozer, `F` (airfield), cancel with a right click.
items.expectation: Every key triggers the button whose label carries the underlined letter: the order appears in the queue, or the building preview hangs on the pointer.

items.title: Placement: preview on a legal and on a refused spot
items.instruction: Strips `placement` and `placement-refused`.
items.expectation: The translucent building hangs on the pointer; on a legal spot in its normal colour, on a building or slope in red.

items.title: Placing and building with the mouse
items.instruction: Select the dozer, press the power plant button, move the preview over the ground, left-click; while it is built place a barracks beside it.
items.expectation: The preview follows the pointer without lag, the click puts the site exactly there, the dozer drives up and builds; a click on forbidden ground gives a message instead of nothing.

items.title: Pointer and waypoints
items.instruction: Pictures `cursor-move` and `waypoints`.
items.expectation: With a unit selected the original's move pointer (green arrows) stands over free ground, not a Windows arrow; waypoints set with Alt are a line with a diamond at every station.

items.title: Pointer changes and rally point in the window
items.instruction: Select a unit and move the pointer over ground, an own building and the command bar; select the war factory and right-click the ground.
items.expectation: The pointer changes without delay (move, select, arrow over the bar) and lies exactly under the hand; the factory gets a rally flag, the next unit first drives out and then there.

items.title: Terrain and start base
items.instruction: Strip of the skirmish start.
items.expectation: Terrain textures blend softly into each other, no tile edges or holes; the command centre has closed, lit walls; the rest of the map is black (unexplored).

items.title: Low camera: walls, selection brackets
items.instruction: Picture `match-lowangle`.
items.expectation: The walls of the command centre are lit, not black; selected buildings carry corner brackets and a bar, the dozer a ring and a bar, and it stands on its tyres.

items.title: Roads
items.instruction: Pictures `roads-junctions`, `roads-crossing`, `roads-overview`.
items.expectation: The roadway is continuous with its centre line, junctions are closed, the edges blend softly into the terrain, the road follows the ground. Where road pieces overlap, the right one lies on top.

items.title: Unexplored terrain
items.instruction: Picture `match-fog`.
items.expectation: Everything is black; no building and no object stands visible in the black.

items.title: Models in the viewer
items.instruction: Pictures `viewer-commandcenter`, `viewer-barracks`, `viewer-crusader`, `viewer-dozer`.
items.expectation: Buildings complete with all walls; the tank with hull, turret and barrel; the dozer with four tyres below and the blade in front.

items.title: Grown base, team colours, shadows
items.instruction: Strip of the skirmish the computer plays.
items.expectation: Buildings and units carry their player's colour, fences stand at the building edges, guns point at their target in a fight. In the original every object casts a shadow on the ground.

items.title: Fog: revealing and darkening in the window
items.instruction: Send the dozer a little way into the black and bring it back.
items.expectation: The terrain is revealed ahead of the unit and darkened (not black again) a short time behind it; both run evenly, without lag or jumps; buildings in the darkened part stay visible with their ground.

items.title: Starting, driving, braking
items.instruction: Watch the tanks and soldiers start and stop.
items.expectation: The movement is smooth and even, without a two-step stutter; tanks are at speed at once (that is what the data say), nothing jumps when it stops.
sources: former 60 Hz list: movement; starting and braking

items.title: Turning
items.instruction: Watch the turn for the way back (after 24 seconds).
items.expectation: Vehicles and soldiers turn steadily into the new direction, not in visible steps and not abruptly.

items.title: Arriving and standing
items.instruction: Watch the moment of stopping.
items.expectation: Every unit stops cleanly, without a twitch afterwards; soldiers change from the walking to the standing animation when they stand and do not walk on the spot.
sources: former 60 Hz list: arrival and rolling out

items.title: A place of one's own at the goal
items.instruction: Watch ten units line up at one goal point.
items.expectation: In the original every unit gets a place of its own beside the goal when the order is given and walks straight there; nobody circles the others or walks in a wide arc around the group.
sources: former 60 Hz list: own goal spot

items.title: Boarding
items.instruction: Watch the five Rangers board the Humvee.
items.expectation: They walk straight to the vehicle and disappear in it as soon as they touch it; nobody walks around the vehicle.

items.title: Leaving a transport
items.instruction: Watch the moment the Humvee stops and the Rangers come out.
items.expectation: In the original the passengers get out beside the vehicle and spread a few steps around it; nobody stands inside the vehicle or inside another soldier.

items.title: Factory exits, America
items.instruction: Command centre, barracks and war factory build three units each (the barracks lies just below the picture: scroll down with the arrow key).
items.expectation: Every unit appears inside its building; where the building has a door it is open then; the unit drives out through the door side (lower right in the picture) by itself and stops in front; the second and third stand beside it, not inside it; the model does not stick through a wall or roof on the way.

items.title: Factory exits, China
items.instruction: As UNIT-07, Chinese buildings.
items.expectation: As UNIT-07. Known: the barracks delivers one Red Guard per order, the original two.

items.title: Factory exits, GLA
items.instruction: As UNIT-07, buildings of the GLA (only the arms dealer has a door).
items.expectation: As UNIT-07.

items.title: War factory up close: door and seat of the model
items.instruction: Strip of the war factory up close.
items.expectation: The door opens before the tank appears and closes after the last one; the tank stands on the floor of the hall when it appears, heading for the door.

items.title: Turrets and fire release
items.instruction: Watch the turrets of the two tanks and of the drone off to the side.
items.expectation: The turret swings steadily onto the enemy and fires only when it points at him; it stays on him until he is dead and turns back calmly two seconds later; the drone glances around now and then while idle.
sources: former 60 Hz list: turrets and fire release

items.title: Projectile paths
items.instruction: Follow the Tomahawk's missile and the Inferno Cannon's shell to the impact.
items.expectation: The missile climbs, turns in and hits the building; the shell flies an arc; both fly smoothly (no stutter), and explosion and fire appear where and when the projectile arrives - not before.

items.title: Jets
items.instruction: Watch two Raptors from their construction to the landing (70 seconds to the landing; the view shows the airfield, the targets lie 700 units to the east - scroll right to see the attack).
items.expectation: The jets taxi to the runway, take off, fly curves instead of turning on the spot, fire their missiles on the approach, circle, land on the runway and taxi to their place.

items.title: Capturing a building
items.instruction: Watch and listen to the Ranger until the barracks changes its colour (28 seconds).
items.expectation: The Ranger walks to the barracks, unpacks, raises the flag; meanwhile the barracks flashes in his colour, faster towards the end, with a tick sound in the same rhythm; then it changes sides.
sources: former 60 Hz list: flashing of the capture

items.title: Wheels, steering, suspension
items.instruction: The Humvee on the zig-zag and the dozer on the straight line.
items.expectation: The wheels turn with the distance, steer into the corner and back afterwards; the dozer nods when it starts and brakes and settles shortly, without trembling.
sources: former 60 Hz list: suspension and steering

items.title: Repair and the wrench symbol
items.instruction: The dozer repairs the damaged power plant (it takes 26 seconds).
items.expectation: The power plant looks damaged; the wrench stands over it while it is repaired and disappears when it is whole; from half health on the building looks undamaged again.

items.title: Construction
items.instruction: The dozer builds a power plant and a barracks.
items.expectation: The dozer drives to the site; the building rises evenly and neither burns nor smokes nor looks ruined while it does (the original shows no damage states during construction); finished it stands complete in the player's colour.

items.title: Muzzle flashes
items.instruction: Watch the barrels of the Gattling and the rifles.
items.expectation: With every shot the muzzle flashes briefly - no constant glow and not just one flash at the beginning; the Gattling spins up and then fires faster.
sources: former 60 Hz list: muzzle flash, firing state

items.title: Tracers and hits
items.instruction: Watch the lines between shooter and target and the men who are hit.
items.expectation: Tracers run from the muzzle to the target; the hit fall with a death animation and lie for a moment.

items.title: Explosions, smoke, wreck
items.instruction: Watch the impacts and the death of the Battlemaster (after 13 seconds).
items.expectation: Every impact gives one short explosion with smoke at the tank that is hit, when the shell arrives; in the original the destroyed tank blows up, its turret flies off and a burning wreck stays for about 20 seconds.

items.title: Flames, smoke and burning
items.instruction: Watch the Dragon tank, the barracks, the power plant and the buggy.
items.expectation: The Dragon tank throws a stream of fire with a burning trail (no box flies); the barracks burns with flames on it while it is aflame; the damaged power plant smokes and burns at several places; the rocket buggy raises dust while it drives; rockets leave a smoke trail.

items.title: Smoke trails and fire at the impact
items.instruction: Watch the missile's smoke trail and the fire of the Inferno shell.
items.expectation: The missile draws a continuous smoke trail that does not break; where the Inferno shell lands it burns for a few seconds.

items.title: Shot and impact sounds
items.instruction: Listen to the tank duel (or play the page's sound capture).
items.expectation: One bang per shot and one impact, in time with the picture; nothing doubled, nothing missing, no crackling.

items.title: Fire fight: many sounds at once
items.instruction: Listen to the fire fight.
items.expectation: Rifles and Gattling can be told apart; it does not clip or distort.
sources: DEMO-FINDINGS no. 7: clipping in longer fights

items.title: Tick sound of the capture
items.instruction: Listen together with UNIT-14.
items.expectation: The tick falls together with every flash of the barracks and gets faster with it.

items.title: Construction and Eva
items.instruction: Listen while it is built.
items.expectation: A construction sound during the work; when the building is finished Eva announces it once, not several times and not at the start of the scene.
sources: DEMO-FINDINGS no. 7: Eva at game start

items.title: Music, unit voices, Eva in a skirmish
items.instruction: In the skirmish: listen, click the dozer, give it an order, build something.
items.expectation: The music of the own side plays; the unit answers the selection and the order with one line each; Eva announces construction and finished units; a refused order gives an error sound.

items.title: Sound of the mission scripts
items.instruction: Listen together with MISS-02.
items.expectation: The typewriter of the captions types audibly; speech and music of the scripts set in fitting the picture.

items.title: Building a base
items.instruction: Build a power plant, a barracks, a supply centre and a war factory, order two units each.
items.expectation: Everything can be built as in the original: buttons unlock with their prerequisites, money drops, units come out of the buildings, the Chinook fetches supplies and the money rises.

items.title: Fighting
items.instruction: March to the enemy (upper right part of the map) with what you built, or wait for his attack; let them fight.
items.expectation: Units attack on a right click and, when idle, by themselves whatever comes into range; a message and an announcement when under fire; the AI builds a base and sends units.

items.title: A skirmish the computer plays
items.instruction: Go through the strip over four minutes of game time.
items.expectation: The base grows sensibly (power plant, barracks, supplies, factory), units gather outside the buildings, nothing stands inside something else.
sources: docs/CLIENT-OBJECTS.md: infantry in the footprint of the depot

items.title: Start and readability
items.instruction: First picture: player 1's base without fog, the header.
items.expectation: Both factions, money and game time are readable in the header (size, contrast); the panel on the left is not cut off.

items.title: Panels and buttons
items.instruction: Press `P`, `U`, `L`, `E`; click every button of the lower bar once; click the radar.
items.expectation: The tab changes, the pictures fit the names, progress bars run; every button does what it says; a click on the radar moves the view.

items.title: Zoom and overview
items.instruction: Mouse wheel far back; `O` and `O` again.
items.expectation: It goes far beyond the usual zoom without flicker, missing objects or tiles; `O` shows the whole map, the second `O` returns to the same place.

items.title: Fog views
items.instruction: Press `F` three times.
items.expectation: Everything, then only what player 1 sees, then only what player 2 sees, then everything; radar and world show the same each time.

items.title: The AI's camera
items.instruction: `F1`, later `F2`; `J`/`K`; an arrow key.
items.expectation: The view follows the blue frame of the radar and shows what the AI is doing (building site, barracks, attack); following is calm and does not jump all the time; the arrow key releases it.

items.title: Speed, pause, no orders
items.instruction: Space, `4`, `8`, `1`; left and right clicks on units and ground.
items.expectation: Space pauses, 4 and 8 speed up, at eight times the picture stays smooth; clicks select nothing and order nothing.

items.title: End of the match
items.instruction: Let it run to the victory with `8` (about five minutes of game time).
items.expectation: The winner is announced at the top, the game stands still, and the losses on the panel fit what was seen.

items.title: The AI builds vehicles and gathers
items.instruction: China against GLA at four times speed; follow the Chinese AI with `F1`, panel `U`.
items.expectation: Once the war factory stands, Battlemasters, Gattlings and Dragons come out of it; at the rally point the units stand in rows side by side, nobody circles another; soldiers told to board a troop crawler get in.
sources: former 60 Hz list: the AI builds vehicles, own goal spot, boarding

items.title: Chance and repeatability
items.instruction: Close the window after a minute and start it again with `r`; compare the two seeds printed. (`pwsh scripts/demo-spectator.ps1 -Seed <number>` runs the same match again.)
items.expectation: Two starts without a seed give different seeds and a different course; the same seed gives the same course.

items.title: Intro of the mission GC_ChemGeneral
items.instruction: Watch the first 30 seconds without clicking.
items.expectation: The camera travels over the base for 25 seconds (soft pans, no jumps), the command bar is hidden meanwhile; then it appears and the mouse works.

items.title: Intro of MD_USA01: texts, fades, counters
items.instruction: Watch and listen to the first minute.
items.expectation: Captions type character by character with a typing sound, stand readable and disappear; fades are soft; camera moves end when the text goes on.

items.title: Building after the intro
items.instruction: After the intro select the dozer and build a power plant.
items.expectation: The dozer builds as in a skirmish; clicks during the intro did nothing.

items.title: The mission's scripts run
items.instruction: Play or watch for two minutes.
items.expectation: The map's enemy acts (attacks, announcements, captions); the mission does not feel like an empty map.

items.title: Movement: 60 Hz against 30 Hz
items.instruction: Press `c` to see the same scene at 30 Hz.
items.expectation: At 60 Hz the movement is visibly smoother; paths, speed and arrival times are the same.

items.title: Effects and sound: 60 Hz against 30 Hz
items.instruction: Press `c` to see and hear the same scene at 30 Hz.
items.expectation: Explosions, smoke and muzzle flashes last as long and are as dense; the same number of shots and sounds.

items.title: Capture: 60 Hz against 30 Hz
items.instruction: Press `c` for the same scene at 30 Hz.
items.expectation: The barracks flashes equally often at both rates (49 times) and changes sides at the same moment.
sources: former 60 Hz list: flashing of the capture

items.title: Mission intro: 60 Hz against 30 Hz
items.instruction: Press `c` for the same intro at 30 Hz.
items.expectation: The camera move takes the same time and ends at the same place.

items.title: Roads: 60 Hz against 30 Hz
items.instruction: Compare the road pictures of both rates side by side.
items.expectation: Known: where road pieces overlap, a different one can lie on top at 30 and at 60 Hz. The question is which picture looks right.

items.title: Smoothness in a skirmish
items.instruction: Mind the feel during SKIRM-01/02.
items.expectation: Scrolling and movement stay smooth while building and fighting; no hitches of noticeable length.

items.title: Loading time
items.instruction: Count along when each window starts.
items.expectation: About half a minute passes from the start to the first picture; the window stays empty in that time. Is that acceptable?

items.title: Spectator at eight times speed
items.instruction: During SPEC-06/07.
items.expectation: At eight times the picture stays smooth, the game does not visibly fall behind.
